BLOCKER: Implement/fix prompts receive `implementation_mandates` + `_implementation_controls_block` only when `_tool_directive` returns non-empty; the `else` and template branches build implement/fix prompts with no mandates and no control contract, so AC2 ("implement/fix prompts include all five") fails on those paths.

No test assembles a real prompt: tests call `implementation_mandates()`/`design_spec_mandates()` directly, so the design_pack failure_behavior ("prompt lacks mandates fails test") is unmet — deleting the injection wiring in `agent_runner` still passes the suite.
MAJOR: Control contract "when present" is untested: only the absent/STOP path is asserted; no test renders `_implementation_controls_block` with rows, so regressions in the binding contract formatting are invisible to AC2.

Design mandates are gated by brittle agent-id heuristics (`startswith("design")`, `"spec" in agent_id`) and only in the `spec.instructions` branch; design/spec agents reaching the template branch get no mandates, leaving AC1 path-dependent.

Bare `except Exception: item = None` around the backlog lookup silently disables contract lookup (e.g. missing `re`, DB outage) and the resulting warning falsely reports "no rows found", conflating infrastructure failure with a genuinely missing matrix.
MINOR: Tech-stack checks read from `config/implementation-controls.json` are wrapped in `except Exception: pass`; "binding" checks can vanish with no log/metric — weak observability for a fail-closed contract.
`design_spec_mandates(agent_id)` / `implementation_mandates(agent_id)` accept an ignored parameter, an API surface implying per-agent variation that never exists; callers pass it for nothing.

New shipped logic (`_implementation_controls_block`, mandate rendering) added in Python; sanctioned by the approved affected_files but in tension with the "new shipped logic -> Go" rule — keep this layer thin.

Local imports (`re` assumed module-level, `from core import backlog`, `import json`) inside the prompt hot path; a `NameError` would be swallowed by the same broad `except`, silently dropping content.
NIT: `docs/PROMPT-MANDATES.md` duplicates the mandate wording verbatim; declare `prompt_builder` constants as the source of truth to prevent doc/code drift.
`.format(id=...)` shadows the builtin `id` and uses a different string style than the adjacent f-string.

`test_code_prompt_stops_without_control_matrix` relies on `BI-PF-9999` never resolving in any backlog backend (file or `PF_BACKLOG_DB=on`); a task string with no ID would be deterministic by construction.

Control-matrix fields are interpolated raw into the prompt with no sanitization; fine today (internally authored), but it contradicts the "no caller-controlled inputs" security claim if design-pack content ever becomes externally sourced.
SUMMARY: Mandate text and the fail-closed warning exist and are partly tested, but the wiring is conditional and untested: implement/fix prompts on non-directive/template paths omit mandates entirely, and no test builds an actual prompt, so both ACs are only partially demonstrable.
Top risks: silent exception handling masking contract absence, brittle agent-id matching for design mandates, and zero coverage of the contract-present rendering path.
